title: Corestats.pro API — Draft Extraction Guide for Google AI Studio

overview.description: This document explains how to programmatically extract draft data (brawler bans, brawler picks, map names, team names, player names, scores, and round info) from the BSC 2026 August tournament brackets on corestats.pro.
overview.scope: The method works identically across all 4 regions (EMEA, NA, SA, EA) and both qualifier days (QD1, QD2) — 8 brackets total for August 2026.

prerequisites: A browser session on https://corestats.pro (the API is protected by Cloudflare — direct curl or fetch from outside the browser may be blocked)
JavaScript execution capability (browser console, Puppeteer, Playwright, or similar)
The ability to make fetch() requests from within the corestats.pro page context

brackets.description: All 8 brackets are for August 2026. Each has a unique UUID used in API calls.
brackets.note: You can also get these dynamically by calling the list endpoint (see below).

api_note: All endpoints are called from within the corestats.pro page (same origin).

endpoints.name: Get Draft Data for a Single Match (Bans, Picks, Maps)
endpoints.description: This is the most important endpoint. It returns the full draft data for one match: bans, picks, maps, game modes, and per-game results.
endpoints.critical_warning: The data[] array contains MULTIPLE entries — one per map/mode played. A Best-of-3 match that went 2-1 will have 3 entries in data[]. If you only use data[0], you will miss the 2nd and 3rd games. You MUST iterate over ALL entries in data[].
endpoints.note: Within each data[i], the games array has 2 entries that are exact duplicates of each other. Only use games[0].

key_data_paths.want: Which team is team 1 vs team 2

critical_gotchas.explanation: One per map/mode. Iterate ALL of them to get every game. Using only data[0] will miss games 2 and 3 in BO3 matches.

critical_gotchas.issue: games[0] and games[1] are identical duplicates
critical_gotchas.explanation: Within each data[i], the games array has 2 entries that are exact copies of each other. Only use games[0].

endpoints.bans_note: Bans are per-map — each data[i] entry has its own teams[].bans[]. Different maps in the same match will have different bans. This is correct behavior, not a bug.

extraction_code.description: Complete extraction functions that correctly handle all the gotchas. Run this in the browser console while on https://corestats.pro.

full_workflow.description: Extract one complete bracket in 3 steps.

match_counts_note: Not all matches have draft data. Matches that are byes (one team advances automatically) or forfeits will return empty data[] from /api/match/live/. These should be skipped or stored with empty games arrays.

game_modes_and_maps.note: All 4 regions use the same pool of game modes and maps.

why_browser_required.reason: The corestats.pro API is protected by Cloudflare. Direct HTTP requests from outside the browser (e.g., Python requests, curl, Node.js fetch) will typically be blocked with a Cloudflare challenge page.
why_browser_required.solution: The browser session on corestats.pro has valid Cloudflare cookies. When you call fetch('/api/...') from within the page context (browser console, Puppeteer page.evaluate(), Playwright page.evaluate()), the request includes these cookies and bypasses the Cloudflare challenge.

requirements: Browser automation capability — Puppeteer, Playwright, or Selenium to navigate to corestats.pro and execute JavaScript in the page context. This is required to bypass Cloudflare.
The API documentation in this guide — the 3 endpoints, the JSON paths, and the two critical gotchas (multiple data[] entries and duplicate games[] entries).
The extraction JavaScript code — the extractDraft() and fetchAllDrafts() functions provided can be used directly or adapted.

can_do: Parse the extracted JSON data (once extracted via browser)
Analyze draft patterns, ban rates, pick rates, win rates
Generate statistics and insights across all 8 brackets
